newsitem.title: USA: Sinatra released from Los Angeles hospital.
newsitem.headline: Sinatra released from Los Angeles hospital.

text.p: Legendary entertainer Frank Sinatra was released from a Los Angeles hospital on Saturday, casting doubt on speculation that he was seriously ill with heart problems.

Sinatra's publicist, Susan Reynolds, said the 80-year-old singer went home from Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre eight days after being admitted for treatment of what was officially described as a pinched nerve.
"He is very happy to be home and again thanks everyone throughout the world for the wonderful get-well wishes he has received," Reynolds said.
Sinatra's departure from the hospital followed a weeklong frenzy of speculation about his condition, with news reports ranging from worsening pneumonia to heart failure.
One day before his release, a Los Angeles TV station had even reported that his hospital room resembled an intensive-care unit.
A source close to Sinatra said he had, in fact, developed a slight case of pneumonia but was almost fully recovered. "There's been a lot of exaggeration about his condition," the source said.
When Sinatra entered Cedars-Sinai on Nov. 1, his publicist and hospital officials said he was there for treatment of a pinched nerve.
Sinatra was originally expected to go home last weekend, but an unexplained extension of his hospital stay fuelled a wave of sometimes conflicting rumours of more serious health problems.

Los Angeles TV station KCBS reported on Friday that his condition was worsening and he was being treated for pneumonia and "heart failure." It said he wanted to go home anyway, against his doctor's advice.
Another local station, KNBC, reported the medicine Sinatra was given for his pneumonia caused an irregular heartbeat but that he was up and walking around and in no grave danger.
Asked about those reports on Saturday, Reynolds declined comment except to say, "It was the doctor who released him."
Sinatra was reportedly annoyed over all the speculation about his health, and he asked his publicists and hospital officials to keep a tight lid on information about his condition.
"We wish you an immediate recovery," comedian Bob Hope said on Friday while Sinatra was still in the hospital. "Get out of there."
The hospital received dozens of flower displays and hundreds of letters for Sinatra during his stay.
Cedars-Sinai was also besieged by reporters and camera crews, and some fans visited the hospital in search of news about his condition.

Sinatra was believed to have returned to one of his homes in the Los Angeles area. He sold his estate near Palm Springs about 1-1/2 years ago and moved to residences in Beverly Hills and Malibu, reportedly to be closer to his family.
